column1: # THE CURATED LAYER over upstream CMUdict — every hand correction to g2p-dict.tsv, made explicit.
# ⚠ `tools/english/en_g2p_ngram.ts --emit` REGENERATES g2p-dict.tsv FROM $CMUDICT, which would silently
# revert every row below. This file is the record that makes that loss visible and recoverable: after an
# --emit, re-apply these rows before shipping the dict. See #1295.
# ⚠ IT IS ALSO THE GATE'S INPUT. test/en-curation-gap.test.ts holds each word out of the dict and asks the
# OOV path what it predicts; a row whose OOV answer is the UPSTREAM shape is a LIVE SPLIT — the engine
# answers one way for the listed word and another for an unlisted word in the same environment.
# LETTER-NAME SPELLINGS. Eight CMUdict rows spell an initialism letter by letter but give one letter its
# SOUND instead of its NAME. Five of them are ⟨g⟩ as [G IY] "ghee" where CMUdict's own `g` row is
# [JH IY] "jee" — so the dictionary contradicts itself, and `GDP` came out ɡˌiːdˌiːpʰˈiː. Found by
# checking every acronym-shaped row against the dict's OWN single-letter readings; after allowing the
# documented ⟨a⟩ exception (letterNameExceptions), these eight were all that disagreed.
# ⚠ `gps` ALREADY READ CORRECTLY and is still fixed here: it is in `acronymLetters`, which spells from
# the letter rows and bypasses its own bad entry. The defect was invisible from the output alone.
# ⚠ THE AUDIT'S "AT MOST TWO DIFFERING PHONES" BOUND IS LOAD-BEARING, not a convenience. Dropped, it also
# returns `lb` [P AW1 N D], `hz` [HH ER1 T Z], `blvd`, `aug`, `mt`, `ct`, `dr`, `msgr` — abbreviation
# GLOSSES, where CMUdict gives the EXPANSION rather than a letter spelling, which is correct for them.
# The bound is what separates "a letter spelling with one letter wrong" from "not a letter spelling".
# ⚠ `acog` IS THE SAME FAULT ONE STEP IN. It is not spelled out letter by letter — it is an acronym said as
# a word, "AY-kog" — but its FIRST letter still carries its NAME, and CMUdict's [AH0 K AO1 G] reads it as the
# reduced article instead ("uh-KOG") and moves the stress to the second syllable to match. Found by diagnosing
# undetermined wikipron divergences one at a time; the referee has eɪkɑɡ.
# ⚠ AND `ia` [IY1 AH0] IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. It is the only other row inside the bound, and it is
# ambiguous: "ee-uh" is a plausible NAME reading, and whether ⟨IA⟩ is Iowa, an initialism, or a name is
# not something the dictionary row can settle. Left alone rather than guessed at.

# `holm`, `ensign` the rank vs the flag, `lower` the verb vs the scowl). These are the rows where the
# ⚠ `bancroft` BELONGS ON THIS LIST ON THE EVIDENCE AND IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, because the dictionary is
# the wrong mechanism for it and a row here would be INERT. Both referees read `bænkɹɔft`, and the reason
# is a compound seam — `Ban·croft`, where the nasal ends the first element and never assimilated. But the
# converter derives `ŋ` from N before K/G itself, gated only on a TRANSPARENT PREFIX, so changing the
# dictionary's `NG` to `N` changes nothing about what is said: `en_rebuild_lexicon.mts --diff` listed
# every other row below and not this one. Fixing it needs a seam-aware guard in the converter, which is
# its own block; recorded here so the next reader does not spend the edit a second time.

# misaki gold reads `champaign` with tʃ and `clio` as kliːoʊ. Both referees and the dictionaries say

column1: # CONSONANT DEFECTS FOUND BY A SKELETON PROBE. An accent difference is a vowel or a rhotic; a spelling
# trap is a CONSONANT. Comparing the CONSONANT SKELETON of our reading against Moby's and the en-GB
# referee's — which is what makes a non-rhotic referee admissible for a GenAm lexical fact — leaves 433
# dictionary words where both referees agree on a skeleton that is not ours. These are the rows from
# three of its classes where two or more INDEPENDENT sources back the referees.
# ⚠ NO INTERNAL MAJORITY FOR THE ITALIAN `-zz-` CLASS, which is why this is a list of words and not a
# rule. Our dictionary splits 44 to 64 on whether `-zz[aeio]` is /ts/ or /z/ AFTER these corrections
# (41 to 67 before them) — `intermezzo` already carried `T S` while `palazzo` carried `Z` — so it is
# inconsistent without being wrong in a direction, and the ~108 Italian surnames in the class have no
# evidence either way. Per-word referee agreement is the only bar that holds there.
# ⚠ THAT IS TRUE OF THE SURNAME CLASS AND FALSE OF THESE WORDS, and the first draft said the stronger
# thing. Our own dictionary already reads the corrected way across the immediate family of most of
# them: `achaea` has K; `distich`, `hemistich`, `tetrastich`, `stichomythia` have K; `neogaea` and
# `notogaea` have JH; `gibber` has JH; `hemorrhage`/`-ed`/`-ing` have JH; `palazzi`, `palazzola`,
# `dipiazza` have `T S`. Held out, the n-gram already predicts the corrected consonant for `stich`,
# `palazzo` and `astilbe`. The evidence here is better than "two referees said so".
# ⚠ THREE CANDIDATES WERE DROPPED, and for each the strongest evidence is the piece the first draft
# did NOT cite: `reg` — wikipron-US, the primary referee, positively reads `ɹ ɛ ɡ`, confirming our row,
# and the en-GB referee carries `ɹɛɡ` as well as `ɹɛd͡ʒ`; `hegemonic` — the en-GB referee likewise
# carries `hɛɡɪmɒnɪk`, and gold's `hˌɛɡəmˈɑnɪk` matches our row phone for phone; `ich` — the two
# ⚠ AND `cham` WAS DROPPED ON A WRONG READING AND IS NOW FIXED. The stated reason was "the referees
# disagree"; in fact Moby reads `kæm`, the en-GB referee carries `kæm` as its second variant, and

column1: # A PROPER NOUN WHOSE CONSONANTS ARE WRONG. GenAm variation is overwhelmingly VOCALIC — a proper noun
# where both independent referees agree against us on the CONSONANT SKELETON is an import defect, not an
# accent. Derived mechanically, not by eye: of the 724 audit candidates, 158 have no lower-case Moby
# headword at all (so Moby knows the word only as a name), and of those 158 exactly 38 differ from the
# agreed reading once every vowel is dropped and ER is folded to R. Of the 38: 31 are taken VERBATIM
# from the agreed reading, `mosel` takes only its consonant, `kilauea` comes from a third source, and
# five are refused. 31 rows therefore leave the candidate list; `mosel` and `kilauea` stay on it by
# design, because agreeing with the referees was never the goal — being right was.
# ⚠ THE SKELETON TEST IS A SIEVE, NOT A VERDICT. Each row was adjudicated by hand against a third
# source, and the five refusals are the reason the test cannot be run as a sweep:
#   `tours`   — the sources mean the French city; at rank 2095 running text means the plural of `tour`,
#               and our T UH1 R Z is right for it. The same trap as `batman` in #1373.
#   `salamis` — THE SAME TRAP, AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS BLOCK FELL INTO IT. Moby and gold carry only
#               `Salamis` the Greek island; running text means the plural of `salami`, which the OOV
#               path already decodes correctly. Being off the frequency list is not evidence the plural
#               is rare — `g2p-common.txt` carries `salami` and simply does not list its plural.
#   `celtic`  — /s/ and /k/ are both live in GenAm and the /s/ is what the sports clubs carry.
#   `julian`  — IY0 AH0 vs Y AH0 is the compression alternation, not a consonant defect; both standard.
#   `deutschland` — the agreed final T is German devoicing, which English does not import here.
# ⚠ THE AGREEMENT RELATION IS STRESS-BLIND, so a row applied VERBATIM imports GOLD'S stress on gold's
# authority alone — `normalise` strips stress before comparing, so Moby never voted on it. 11 of the 33
# move primary stress and ONE OF THE 11 WAS WRONG: `mosel` went to the final-stressed `moselle` reading,
# making two distinct names byte-identical. Its row now takes the CONSONANT and keeps our stress, which
# is the general rule this block should have started from — apply only what the agreement can see.
# ⚠ `cointreau` KEEPS ITS FINAL STRESS ONLY BECAUSE IT ALREADY HAD IT. Moby's own body is initial
# (`'kw/A/ntr/oU/`) and gold is final, so the sources are 1–1 and the audit could not tell; the applied
# change is the ⟨oin⟩ glide, and the stress is untouched rather than adjudicated.
# ⚠ `kilauea` IS THE ONE ROW NOT TAKEN FROM THE AGREED READING. Both referees agree with each other and
# BOTH disagree with M-W (kē-lə-ˈwā-ə) on the first vowel, where OURS is right — so the agreed form
# would have imported a wrong vowel to fix a right consonant. A first draft refused the row on the
# grounds that "no source carries" the needed form, in the same sentence that cited M-W carrying it.
# The row is M-W's complete reading; our old row disagreed with it in two places and agreed in one.
# ⚠ `bengal` IS IN THE 38 ONLY INCIDENTALLY. Its skeleton difference is NG G vs N G, which the audit's
# own never-a-defect predicate would reject — the predicate compares whole strings, and here the stress
# and vowel differ too, so it did not fire. The defect being fixed is the stress AND the second vowel
# ⚠ `bengals` IS DELIBERATELY LEFT AT `B EH1 NG G AH0 L Z`, breaking the paradigm on purpose. Neither
# referee carries it, so the audit never saw it and this is not two sources agreeing with us; it is a
# judgement that running text means the NFL team, which is `ˈbɛŋɡəlz`. Stated because a silent paradigm
# split is indistinguishable from an oversight.
# ⚠ `brobdingnagian`, `cointreau` and `homs` ARE NOT BELOW. They already carry a curated row from the
# LOT/THOUGHT block; their rows are updated in place, because no word may hold two curated rows.

column1: # THE STRESS AXIS — 238 rows adjudicated by `tools/english/en_stress_compare.mts`, plus 101 taken so a
# paradigm does not split. The segmental audit cannot see this class AT ALL: its `normalise()` strips
# stress before comparing, so no pure stress error has ever been one of its candidates, and its own
# `iə / jə` predicate says so in a comment about `eosinophilia`. This is the same two referees on the
# same population, projected the other way — the segments already agreed, and what is compared is
# ⚠ ONLY THE PRIMARY MOVES. The `curated` column is OUR row with one digit promoted and the vacated
# primary demoted to a secondary — it is NOT gold's row. Gold's row also carries gold's segments and
# gold's secondaries, and this relation adjudicates neither: inside the compared bucket gold marks a
# secondary we do not on 2,942 words against 1,271 the other way, which is a notation convention and
# not a defect class. #1377 earned this rule from the opposite direction, where a stress-BLIND
# agreement moved the primary on 11 rows and got `mosel` wrong.
# ⚠ SIX OF THE 238 ARE MALFORMED ROWS RATHER THAN MISPLACED ONES — `antipode`, `gasify`, `polyglot`,
# `tonsil`, `rehab` (rank 8,050) and `nympho` carried a secondary and NO primary, so they shipped with no
# tonic at all: `the antipode of gold` → `ðə ˌæntɪpʰˌoᶷd ʌv ɡˈoᶷɫd`. A first version of the instrument
# scored such a row at nucleus 0 "because `enforceSinglePrimary` promotes the first vowel" and so declared
# these six in AGREEMENT with the referees. That function does not run on the dictionary path at all — its
# own comment asserts "a dictionary row always has one", an invariant 103 rows violate — and the thing that
# can rescue the word, `promoteFirstVowel` in `english.ts`, is CLAUSE-scoped and usually does not fire.
# Any tonic beats none, so a malformed row is a candidate wherever the referees agree it goes.
# ⚠ THE 101 PARADIGM ROWS HAVE NO REFEREE AND ARE TAKEN ANYWAY. `decade` is adjudicated and `decades`
# is not in the referees' intersection, so correcting only the lemma would ship `DEC-ade` against
# `de-CADES` — the `bengals` split of #1377, silent and indistinguishable from an oversight.
# INFLECTION never moves the primary, so the move is mechanical. DERIVATION can (`government` →
# `governmental`), so derived forms are deliberately NOT propagated to; `handcraft` keeps its
# fore-stress under a corrected `handcrafted` for exactly that reason.
# ⚠ AND THE SWEEP NEEDS E-ELISION, WHICH A FIRST VERSION DID NOT HAVE. Concatenating alone looks
# `overcome` + `ing` up as `overcomeing`, finds nothing, and reports the paradigm clean — while the
# dictionary carries `overcoming` fore-stressed against a corrected `over·COME`. Ten `-ing` rows plus
# `anchovies` and `rhinoplasties` (consonant + y → -ies) were shipping that way. The enumerator and the
# sweep now live in the tool, not in a scratch file, because a check that gates a 339-row block has to be
# ⚠ AND A SIBLING GOLD RECORDS AS A POS-CONDITIONED HETERONYM IS SKIPPED. `undertaking` is
# `{DEFAULT: ˈʌndəɹtˌAkɪŋ, VERB: ˌʌndəɹtˈAkɪŋ}` in gold; our row is the NOUN and is right. Propagating
# `under·TAKE` into it would have replaced a correct default with the verb reading — the `override` /
# `overriding` shape the curation gate already records, caught only because the guard was added.
# ⚠ THE FREQUENCY LIST IS NOT THE POPULATION — 125 of the 233 candidates are off `g2p-common.txt`
# entirely, and they hold the clearest defects in the set: the productive `-ation`/`-ic`/`-ician`
# suffix classes (`alternation`, `amniotic`, `beautician`). A first cut of this block stopped at the
# ranked head and would have left `beautician` reading ˈbjuːtɪʃən. That is the mistake #1374 fixed for
# the segmental audit, and #1377 restated as "absence from a 40k list is not evidence".
# ⚠ `thereupon` IS THE ONE CANDIDATE REFUSED, and its refutation is gold's own file: gold reads
# `whereupon` wˌɛɹəpˈɑn and `hereupon` hˌɪɹəpˈɑn final-stressed, and `thereupon` ðˈɛɹəpˌɑn initial. A
# source contradicting itself across one word-family is not evidence about that family. Gold's
# INFLECTIONAL self-consistency was checked mechanically across all 233 and is total; this split is
# lexical, so only reading it found it.
# ⚠ `snafus` IS A PARADIGM ROW DROPPED RATHER THAN MOVED. Its dict row is `S N AE1 F AH0 S` where the
# lemma is `S N AE1 F UW0` — a reduced vowel and an unvoiced plural where neither belongs — so moving
# a primary onto it would have written a stressed ʌ into a slot that is already wrong. It is a
# SEGMENTAL defect, which is the other audit's business; recorded there rather than patched here.
